column2: Where can I find all the family’s tracks, albums, plays, films, inventions, terms of office…?
column3: Lists → “🎨 Creations and careers” group: “Everything that was created or lived”, then one list per family (🎵 Music, 🎭 Stage, 🎬 Films and series, 📚 Writings, 🖼 Visual arts, ⚒️ Crafts, 💡 Inventions and discoveries, 🧭 Expeditions, 🏛 Political careers, 🏅 Sport, 🎓 Education, ✎ My types…), for all the people. The same bar as the other lists: 🔍 Search (title, person, place, year), Filter ▾ (kind with the number, person, period, place, with image, with sound or video), List | Cards, Sort. “Group by kind” puts a subheading per kind (“🎵 Tracks (34)”); untick it to mix everything. A click opens the record in the person’s catalogue, “↗” opens the person’s record, “＋ New…” asks for the person then the kind. Press review and Honours list are in the same group.

column2: A person is mentioned as a classmate, jury member or guest in someone else’s record: where can I see it?
column3: On their own record, in the same block: the appearances, awards and stages stored with another person where they appear are shown too, with “in the record of …” and their role. A click opens the record concerned.

column2: Which shapes are there for the decorative tree to print?
column3: Lists → Editing tools → 🌳 Decorative tree → ＋: fan (half circle, 240°, three quarters 270°), wheel, drawn tree (trunk, branches, foliage), tree of boxes from bottom to top, or ancestry table from left to right. Up to 12 generations for the fans and the wheel, 8 for the drawn tree, 7 for the boxes (the number offered follows the shape). The tree then opens in the vector drawing so you can retouch everything.

column2: How do I create my own style or my own size for the decorative tree?
column3: In the tree window: “＋” next to Style (or 🎨 My styles): a name, the starting style, the font, and each colour (paper, ink, title, the person’s box, paternal and maternal sides, empty boxes, trunk, leaves) with a preview. ⚙️ next to Size (or ⚙️ My sizes): your sizes in cm (from 5 to 500), and for all of them, sizes as well as styles, tick the ones you see and arrange them with ↑ ↓. The same settings are in Settings → “Editing, retouching, page layout and sound” → 🌳 Decorative tree, with the shape, size and style offered at the start.

column2: How do I arrange the shapes of the decorative tree or give them a shortcut?
column3: “⚙️ Customise” in the tree window, or Settings → “Editing, retouching, page layout and sound” → Buttons and options → 🌳 Decorative tree: hide or arrange the shapes and buttons. Just below (and in Settings → Keyboard shortcuts), give a key to a shape, to “My sizes”, “My styles” or to “Create the tree”.

column2: How do I choose a custom size for a map (width, height, unit, resolution)?
column3: Lists → Editing tools → 🗺️ Map → “＋ New map”: in “Size”, take a size from the list (A0 to A6, US Letter, postcard, square, 10 × 15, 13 × 18 photos…, 16:9 screens) or “✎ Custom size…”: width × height, the unit (mm, cm, px, inches), ▯ Portrait / ▭ Landscape and the resolution (dpi) for export as an image. The size is remembered for the next map and stored in “⭐ My sizes” (at the top of the list, in all tools); “× Remove from My sizes” takes it away. To print the screen (a map included) in a custom size: 🖨 Print → “✎ Other…”.

column2: How do I change the size of a drawing or a map after creating it?
column3: In the vector drawing: File → “📐 Document size / artboards…” (also in the 📄 Document tab): the size from the shared list or a custom size, the unit, the orientation, the resolution suggested for export, the background (colour or transparent) and the bleed (3 mm at first, added around each page when exporting “with bleed and crop marks”). The objects stay in place, are rescaled with the artboard, or keep their size and are recentred. ↶ (⌘Z) goes back to the previous size; 💾 Save keeps it with the drawing.

column2: Where do I put the title, author or rights of a drawing, a book or a retouched photo?
column3: File → “ℹ️ Information…” in the vector drawing (title, author, subject, description, keywords, rights, language, date: in the exported SVG and PDF), in the page layout (title, author, subject, description, keywords, language and optional ISBN, checked: in the PDF, HTML and ePub) and in photo retouching (title, author, rights, description, keywords, date, linked people: written into the PNG or JPG image, readable by Photoshop, Lightroom or the file explorer). This information is kept with the document; ↶ undoes it.

column2: How do I change the page size of a book I have already started?
column3: In the page layout: File → “📐 Document size…” (or ⚙️ Document tab): page size (shared list or custom size), orientation, facing pages, margins, columns and bleed. “Apply the size to”: all pages, the page shown, or some pages (“2-5, 8”) — a page with its own size prints on a sheet of its size. The objects stay in place or are rescaled. ↶ (⌘Z) goes back; 💾 Save keeps everything.

column2: How do I enlarge or shrink a photo, or add a margin around it?
column3: In photo retouching: Image → “📏 Image size…”: width and height (pixels, %, cm, mm, inches), 🔗 keep proportions, resolution (dpi), resample or not and the method (bicubic smoother for enlarging, sharper for reducing, nearest neighbour to keep sharp pixels); “Fit to a size” takes a size from the shared list. Image → “⬚ Canvas size…” enlarges or crops the canvas around the photo: anchor on 9 points, coloured or transparent background, “Relative” to write what is added. The area appears around the photo and the final size is shown below; everything is applied when you save or export the image, and ↶ undoes it.

column2: How do I rotate a photo (on its side, upside down, mirrored)?
column3: In photo retouching: Image → “🔄 Image rotation”: ↻ 90° clockwise, ↺ 90° anticlockwise, 180°, “Angle…” (a free angle: the canvas grows, transparent or coloured corners, and “✂️ Crop to remove empty corners”), “📐 Straighten the horizon” (draw a line along the horizon or a wall: the angle is suggested automatically), horizontal or vertical flip. The whole image turns as one: layers, masks, selection, texts, shapes, adjustment layers; width and height swap, the resolution stays. A single step: ↶ undoes everything. A phone photo still on its side offers “↻ Put it upright”. The commands can have their own shortcut (⚙️ Customise → retouching shortcuts). In quick retouching: ↺ ↻ in the left column and the Image menu. The original is kept: saving makes a new version.

column2: How do I draw a house to the nearest centimetre?
column3: In the plan, when drawing a wall (▬), a dimension (📏) or a free room: click the starting point then type the length on the keyboard (350, 3.5 m, 35 mm) and Enter; add the angle with @ (350 @ 90: upwards; 0 to the right, 180 to the left). With the room tool (⬚), type “420 x 350”. At the top left: the mouse position, the length and the angle of the current line. 🧲 Snap: grid (1 to 100 cm), corners, middles of walls, along walls, alignments (pink guide lines), angle step (90° to 1°). Alt: without snapping. The arrows move what is selected by 1 cm (⇧: one grid step). In Properties: length, angle and coordinates of walls, distances from a door or window to the ends of the wall, X and Y of furniture.

column2: How do I compare two periods of the house?
column3: In the plan, the 👻 layer menu (next to the floors) offers “🕰 Previous period”, “🕰 Next period” or a period of your choice: the same floor, as it was, appears in sepia dotted lines under the one you are drawing (same transparency as the floors layer). Switch on “Legend: ― added · ┄ gone” in the Floor tab: walls added since are underlined in green, those that have gone are dotted, with their number at the top of the plan. In 3D, the “🕰 Other period” switch shows its walls transparently. With the 🕰 Year slider (🏠 House tab), “👻 Show the previous period as a ghost” always keeps the previous period underneath.

column2: How do I make a mezzanine, a double-height living room or a stairwell?
column3: The simplest: click the room (the living room) then, in Properties → “▨ Floor”, “🏗 Mezzanine open onto this room”: the floor above is added if missing, the mezzanine covers part of the room, the rest becomes a void with its railing, and a staircase arrives at the edge of the mezzanine. By hand: on the floor above, the ▨ “Void” tool (O key) and drag diagonally; or tick “No floor: void onto the floor below” on a room. The plan shows a hatched “VOID”, the floor below “double height” in dotted lines; in 3D the floor is cut open; during the visit you cannot walk into the void. The railing (wood, metal, glass, low wall or none, height of your choice) is placed automatically along the edges without a wall.

column2: How does a staircase cut through the floor above?
column3: A staircase placed (straight, turning, spiral, miller’s ladder) automatically opens the stairwell in the floor of the storey above, with a railing around it except on the arrival side; on the floor above, its outline is drawn in dotted lines with “↓”. Its height follows the floor height plus the thickness of the floor (untick “Height: that of the floor…” to fix it). The panel gives the number of steps, their height and the tread, and warns if the staircase is too steep (Blondel’s rule, 2 h + g between 60 and 66 cm). “⇅ Reverse the direction of climb”, quarter turn to the left or right. For a house drawn before: “Open the stairwells of all staircases”. During the visit, going up you arrive just after the last step.

column2: How do I add dormers, an eyebrow dormer, roof windows (Velux) or gutters?
column3: Floor tab → “🏠 Roof (3D view)”: “＋ Roof window”, “＋ Dormer” (two small slopes) or “＋ Shed dormer” (one slope rising towards the roof). For each: the slope (front or back), its place along the roof, its width and height; × removes it (↶ puts it back). The “Gutters and downpipes” box places them along the eaves. Everything is visible in the 3D view.

column2: My house is L-shaped (or T, U): how do I get the right roof?
column3: Floor tab → “🏠 Roof” → “One roof per wing”. The house is cut into rectangular wings according to its rooms; each one gets its own roof, at the same pitch: where two roofs meet, the valley is made automatically. Dormers then have a “Wing” choice.

column2: How do I make an attic with a sloping ceiling (and the Carrez law area)?
column3: On the top floor, with a sloping roof: Floor tab → “🏠 Attic” → “Attic: the ceiling follows the slope of the roof”, then the height of the low walls (knee wall). The plan hatches the places under 1.80 m, the bottom of the screen gives the ceiling height under the mouse, each room shows its “Carrez law” area, and the 3D view, the section and the visit follow the slope.

column2: How do I make a curved wall (round tower, apse, arched wall)?
column3: Click the wall, then in Properties → “⌒ Curvature (sagitta)”: how far its middle bulges out from the straight line (+ on one side, − on the other; 0 = straight). The plan, 3D, the visit and the section follow the curve: the room’s floor too, the dimension gives the length of the arc and the sagitta, and doors and windows are placed on the curve.
